blocks.prompt: 13 The vector \(\underline{u} = 50\underline{i} + 75\underline{j} + 65\underline{k}\) shows how many belts, pants, and shirts were sold at a store. The vector \(\underline{w} = 1500\underline{i} + 3500\underline{j} + 3000\underline{k}\) shows the price (in rupees) of each item. Find \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\) and explain what the result tells us in real life.
blocks.explanation:
A real-life dot product: quantities times prices.
We must find \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\) and interpret it.
Plan: multiply matching components and add; each product is the money from one item.
steps:
Given: quantities \(\underline{u} = 50\underline{i} + 75\underline{j} + 65\underline{k}\) (belts, pants, shirts); prices \(\underline{w} = 1500\underline{i} + 3500\underline{j} + 3000\underline{k}\) rupees.
To find: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w}\) and its meaning.
Method: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = u_1w_1 + u_2w_2 + u_3w_3\) (14.2.5).

Multiply matching components
\[50 \times 1500 = 75{,}000\]
\[75 \times 3500 = 262{,}500\]
\[65 \times 3000 = 195{,}000\]
Why: Number sold \(\times\) price of one item = money from that item.

Add
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = 75{,}000 + 262{,}500 + 195{,}000\]
\[= 532{,}500\]
Why: The dot product adds the three products.

Meaning and check
\[262{,}500 + 195{,}000 = 457{,}500\]
\[457{,}500 + 75{,}000 = 532{,}500 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Adding in a different order gives the same total. The result is the total revenue (money received) from the sales of all the belts, pants and shirts.
blocks.final_answer: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = 532{,}500\): the store's total revenue from all three items is Rs. 532,500.
